chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazem, from Ibrahim ibn Ma'rudd, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): The people of Kufa narrate from Ali (peace be upon him) that he was in Kufa and urinated until scum appeared, then performed wudu, then wiped on his sandals, then said: This is the wudu of the one who does not invalidate it. He said: Yes, he did that. He said: Then what act of invalidation is more invalidating than urinating? So he said: By that he only meant excessiveness in performing wudu, that one adds onto the limitation of wudu.
ai.seo_question: Does urination invalidate wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a potential ambiguity in Kufan reports regarding whether urination invalidates *wudu*. He explains that the phrase 'this is the wudu of one who has not had a major impurity' refers to avoiding *ta'addi* (excessiveness or going beyond the prescribed limits) in the act of washing itself, rather than suggesting that the act of urination does not break *wudu*. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic interpretation (*ta'wil*) to reconcile apparent contradictions in early hadith transmissions.
